content: In Object Mode, add a Cube. In Edit Mode, go into Face Mode and select the bottom face and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D cursor to the bottom face and then [k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode and [k]RMB > Set Origin > Origin to 3D Cursor[/k] (Image 1). This will place the cube's pivot point on the bottom face. In Edit Mode, [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a vertical Loop Cut to the cube and remove the left half. Add a Mirror Modifier and enable clipping (Image 2). Move the cube to the top of the hips and in Front View scale it down to cover the waist up to the bottom of the rib cage (Image 3). In Side View, adjust the sides to match the contours of the waist (Image 4).

content: In Front View, select the top face and [k]E[/k] to extrude it to the top of the clavicle (Image 5). Add a horizontal Loop Cut and move it to around the thickest part of the chest (Image 6). Adjust the Loop Cut and the top face of the torso to match the contours of the body from the front (Image 7) and the side (Image 8). If you have an image reference for the back, check that as well (Image 9).

content: [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View, select the front outer edge, and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel it to provide some rounding (Image 10). Select the two lower Edge Loops, [k]Numpad3[/k] into side, and [k]R[/k] to add a slight rotation (about -8.5 degrees) (Image 11).

content: [k]Ctrl-Alt-S[/k] to save an incremental version of the file. In Edit Mode select the bottom face of the torso and [k]Shift-D,Z[/k] to create a copy of the face and move it down (Image 13). [k]P,S[/k] to separate the selection into a new object (Image 14). In Edit Mode, select the hips' top face and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the cursor there. Then, in Object Mode, [k]RMB > Set Origin > Origin to 3D Cursor[/k] to move the hips' origin to its top face. Select the torso mesh and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D cursor to the bottom of the torso. Select the cube and [k]RMB > Snap > Selection to Cursor[/k] to move it to just below the torso (Image 14).

content: In Side View, [k]E[/k] to extrude the hips so they come down about halfway down to the middle of the butt (Image 15). Select edges and [k]S[/k] to scale them in the x- and y-axes to shape the hips from the front (Image 16) and side (Image 17).

content: Select the bottom edge and [k]G,Z[/k] to drag it down to the bottom of the crotch (Image 18). [k]Numpad7,Numpad9[/k] to go into Bottom View (Image 19). [k]K[/k] to add edges between the front and the back that form the shape of an 'M' (Image 20). [k]Numpad1,Numpad9[/k] to go into Rear View (Image 19) and [k]K[/k] to add edges between the side and the middle that form a 'V' shape (Image 21).

content: [k]Ctrl-Alt-S[/k] to save an incremental version of the file. Select the bottom face of the hips and move the 3D Cursor there (Image 22). [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View, [k]Shift-A > Mesh > Plane[/k] to add a Plane at the 3D Cursor, [k]S[/k] to scale it in and [k]R,45[/k] to rotate it (Image 23). [k]E[/k] to extrude it to the middle of the knee (Image 24). [k]G[/k], [k]S[/k] to move and scale the edges to match the contours of the thighs in side (Image 25) and front view (Image 26). Extrude the top and bottom faces and [k]S,X,0[/k], [k]S,Y,0[/k] to bring them into a point (Image 27). Finally, add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis using the torso as the Mirror Object (Image 28).

content: [k]Ctrl-Alt-S[/k] to save an incremental version of the file. [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate the thigh mesh and move it down (Image 29). [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and move the bottom Edge Loop up to the middle of the calves (Image 30). Scale the top and bottom Edge Loops to match the contour of the reference image (Image 31). Extrude the bottom Edge Loop down to the bottom of the calf muscle and scale it in (Image 32). Delete the bottom vertex and extrude the bottom Edge Loop to below the ankles (Image 33). Fill the bottom face (Image 34).

content: Add a Cube to the scene and move it in place. Scale it down so the top is above the ankles (Image 35). In Side View, scale the cube to match the foot length (Image 36). Add a vertical Loop Cut that lines up with the calf's edge loop (Image 37). Select the back face and [k]S,X,0[/k] to taper it in (Image 38). Select the front face and [k]S,X[/k] to scale it in (Image 39). [k]G,Z[/k] to raise the Edge Loop on the top face (Image 40). Add a Mirror Modifier (Image 41).

content: [k]Ctrl-Alt-S[/k] to add an incremental save. Add a Cube to the scene and move it up to the shoulder area. Scale it down and rotate 45 degrees around the x-axis (Image 42). In Side View, grab the bottom edge and drag it down to create a kite shape (Image 43). Select the two edges across the middle and [k]S,Y[/k] to scale them out in the y-axis (Image 44). Using the Knife Tool, cut edge loops across the vertices on both sides (Image 45). Select the bottom edge and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel it to create a face from which the upper arm will extend (Image 46). Select the top of the triangle edge created by the bevel and move it up to the center of the cube (Image 47). Extrude the bottom face to the elbow and then again to the wrist (Image 48).

content: Extrude the bottom face to the elbow and then again to the wrist (Image 48). Select all vertices for the lower arm and [k]P,S[/k] to separate them from the shoulder/upper arm (Image 49). Change to editing the lower arm and fill in the top face and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to move the 3D Cursor there and then [k]RMB > Set Origin > Origin to 3D Cursor[/k] to set the pivot point (Image 50). Rotate the lower arm to match the angle of the reference image and write the angle down (Image 51). [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a Loop Cut where the thickest part of the forearm will be (image 52). Scale it up in the y-axis (Image 53). Extrude out the bottom edge for the fist and scale it in slightly (Image 54).
